prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1087; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the individual injured in a collision that occurred in a parking lot. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or electronic means. If your insured or any representative of your company has already made contact with our client, please let us know so that we may address it.

We request that you provide the policy limits of liability coverage applicable to your insured for this incident, along with a copy of the declarations page. Please also confirm whether any other policies, including umbrella or excess coverage, may apply.

We further demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes claim files, photographs, recorded statements, adjuster notes, vehicle data, repair estimates, surveillance footage, and any communications with your insured or third parties. Destruction, alteration, or loss of such materials may expose your company to sanctions and claims of spoliation.

Please acknowledge receipt of this letter in writing within fifteen days so that we may proceed with the claim efficiently.
